neighbours.label: pest or disease name opened by the split piece ' sc'/' st' in biology or agriculture prose (sc|ab, sc|orch, sc|abies, st|ink bug), plus 'various' before environmental stresses
fire: Wet springs leave the potatoes covered in scab by harvest time.
Outbreaks of scabies are common in nursing homes where residents share bedding.
Bacterial leaf scorch has killed hundreds of oaks along the avenue.
Soybean growers lose part of every crop to the brown marmorated stink bug.
The orchard inspector found scab lesions on nearly every pear.
Sailors on the long voyage developed scurvy when the lime ration ran out.
Sheep with scab must be dipped twice a year under the regulations.
The scabby patches on the dog's belly were caused by mites.
quiet: Wet springs leave the potatoes small and watery by harvest time.
Outbreaks of flu are common in nursing homes where residents share rooms.
Powdery mildew has weakened hundreds of oaks along the avenue.
Soybean growers lose part of every crop to aphids and rust.
The foreman would scold anyone who left a scuff on the polished deck.
The captain discovered a stowaway behind the crates in the hold.
The union called the replacement workers scabs and blocked the gate.
Fire blight blackened the pear blossoms within a week.

predictions: 6-7/8 fire (probe: scab 0.957, leaf scorch 0.641, various stimuli 0.601, stink bug 0.501, scabies 0.356); the same pieces outside biology 0.12-0.28 (scold 0.129, stowaway 0.116, labour scabs 0.283) and disease words without the piece near zero
notes: The - pole fires on the same word-initial cluster pieces in Russian and German (' ск', ' Sk', ' sch'), so the neuron splits consonant-cluster openers by language and the + pole adds a pest/disease context. ' bi' (biophysical) scored only 0.077 and was dropped from the label. Near misses test the piece without the disease sense and the disease sense without the piece.
